subject: Post-demo follow-up: trace ID hashing + retention check-in
messages:
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood-inference.com
To: laura.chen@echohealth.com, security@echohealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, ben_carter@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2024-04-22T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: trace ID hashing + retention check-in

Hi Laura / EchoHealth security team — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and the open items we promised to follow up on related to logging and sensitive data handling. I’ve grouped items by ask so it’s easier to review: 

1) Request/response logs (what we persist)
- Current approach we demoed: request and response JSON are captured for debugging but we automatically apply PII scrubbers and header filters before writing to persistent logs.
- Open: Confirmed names/SSNs/medical IDs are removed; you asked about customer-specific fields (e.g., patient_reference) — we can add a transform rule set scoped to your account.

2) Trace IDs / correlation identifiers
- Proposal: we can hash trace IDs on ingest (SHA-256) and store only the last 8 hex chars for quick joins. Full raw trace ids are kept transiently in-memory for live debugging windows (configurable, e.g., 24h) and not persisted after the window.
- You asked whether hashed values are reversible: our hashing is one-way; we do not store keys that allow reversal.

3) Retention windows and environments
- Default: 30 days for structured logs, 7 days for full request/response payloads unless you opt-in to extended retention under a contract.
- We can set shorter windows for prod vs staging per your policy (example: prod 30d, staging 3d).

4) Auditability / evidence for compliance
- We can provide sanitized log examples, redaction playbooks, and a SOC2 artifact list. I’ve attached a small demo logs CSV with redaction markers.

Next steps we propose:
- EchoHealth to confirm whether the last-8-chars approach for hashed trace IDs meets your correlation needs.
- Security to share any minimum retention requirements (legal/regulatory) or required evidence artifacts.
- If acceptable, schedule a short follow-up (30 min) with engineering to walk the exact transform rules and hashing algorithm details.

Attachments: demo-logs-sample.csv (csv)

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa and Ben on engineering follow-up once you confirm the trace ID and retention preference.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood-inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0148

From: "Laura Chen" <laura.chen@echohealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood-inference.com
Cc: security@echohealth.com
Date: 2024-04-22T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: trace ID hashing + retention check-in

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the concise recap. A few clarifying questions from our side before we lock the next steps: 

- Trace IDs: hashing + storing last 8 chars sounds reasonable, but our SREs want to ensure that the last-8 approach will not cause collisions that impede incident correlation across services. Can you share the collision analysis or guidance on collision risk at our scale (approx 2M requests/day)?

- Retention windows: Regs require 90 days for certain audit trails in our environment (we’ll confirm exactly which trails). Would Redwood be able to support selective 90d retention for sanitized metadata (not full payloads) under a DPA addendum?

- Proof of redaction: Legal wants a sanitized sample showing the redaction pipeline applied to PII (preferably from staging data or a clearly synthetic sample).

- Chain of custody: we need to understand who can access unhashed trace IDs during the transient debugging window and what access controls / audit logs are in place.

I attached a short list of legal/security questions. Let us know your availability for a follow-up call with product engineering and our SRE lead, on either Thu 4/25 or Mon 4/29.

[Attachment: Echo_Health_Legal_Qs.docx]

Best,
Laura Chen
Head of Security Operations
EchoHealth
laura.chen@echohealth.com

---
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood-inference.com
To: laura.chen@echohealth.com, security@echohealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com, ben_carter@redwood-inference.com
Date: 2024-04-22T17:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: trace ID hashing + retention check-in

Laura — thanks for the questions, useful level of detail. Quick answers inline and then proposed ops next steps. 

- Collision risk: for last-8 hex chars we expect ~16^8 possibilities (~4.2 billion). At 2M reqs/day the collision probability is extremely low for daily joins but non-zero over long windows. If you need stronger uniqueness we can: (a) increase stored suffix to last 12 chars, or (b) keep a short monotonic request counter per customer for deterministic joins. Option (b) avoids relying on suffix entropy and we can scope it to EchoHealth only.

- 90d selective retention: yes — Redwood supports selective retention for sanitized metadata under an enterprise DPA. We would keep only non-PII metadata for 90d and redact payloads to standard 7d unless otherwise specified in contract.

- Proof of redaction: I’ll ask Marissa to produce a synthetic-but-realistic sanitized sample exported from a staging run. That will include before/after markers and the exact transform rules applied.

- Chain of custody / access controls: short summary: only SRE and Platform engineers on a need-to-know roster can request transient access; requests are gated via the console (approval flow) and every access is logged in audit events (user, timestamp, reason). We do not keep raw trace IDs in persistent storage. I’ve pasted a short snippet of the access control policy here: 

"Transient debug access: TTL limited tokens (max 24h by default), just-in-time approval, automatic audit log entry for each session."

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa will share a sanitized sample + transform rules (ETA: EOD 4/23).
2) Ben will confirm hashing vs suffix-length options with infra and propose default (ETA: 4/24).
3) If EchoHealth confirms 90d metadata retention, we’ll prepare DPA addendum language and scope matrix.
4) Schedule a 30-min technical call — I’m available Thu 4/25 10–11am PT or Mon 4/29 2–3pm PT. Which works for your SRE lead?

Link to demo notes and our logging doc: https://app.redwood-inference.com/docs/logging-redaction#traceid-hashing

Thanks — looping Marissa and Ben.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
